gloss: New Year's Eve; the last night of the year

definitions.gloss: New Year's Eve; the last night of the year
definitions.explanation: The night of December 31st. Most commonly encountered in the compound {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね} (the New Year's Eve temple bells).

examples.japanese: {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}が{鳴|な}る。
examples.english: The New Year's Eve bells ring.

examples.japanese: {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}は108{回|かい}{撞|つ}かれる。
examples.english: The New Year's Eve bells are struck 108 times.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}を{聞|き}きながら{新年|しんねん}を{迎|むか}えるのが{我|わ}が{家|や}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: It's our family's custom to welcome the new year while listening to the New Year's Eve bells.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね} is one of the most iconic sounds of the Japanese New Year. Buddhist temples ring their bells 108 times — once for each of the 108 worldly desires ({煩悩|ぼんのう}) in Buddhist teaching. The ringing begins on the night of December 31st and often continues past midnight into the new year. It is broadcast on TV as part of NHK's {紅白|こうはく}{歌合戦|うたがっせん} end-of-year programming.

ETYMOLOGY:
{除|じょ} means "to remove" and {夜|や} means "night." The name refers to the night that removes the old year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね} (New Year's Eve bells — the most common use by far)
- {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}を{撞|つ}く (to ring the New Year's Eve bells)
- {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}を{聞|き}く (to listen to the New Year's Eve bells)
